target: General SWE / backend software engineering internships (big tech + strong startups), 2026-27 cycle

bullet_feedback.bullet: Writing Java policies that tune upper/lower bounds on EC2 capacity reserved for Amazon Redshift operations like patching, balancing availability against cost; initial backtests complete
bullet_feedback.problem: "Java policies" next to "EC2" reads to an AWS-trained screener (and to an LLM screener) as IAM/access policies, not capacity-allocation logic. The bullet is about a control/optimization algorithm, but the word chosen points to permissions config.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the top line under the strongest brand on the page; if it is misread as writing permission policies, the algorithmic work (bounding reserved capacity against cost) is lost.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what a 'policy' is here (the code module that decides how much capacity to reserve?)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Replace "policies" with a noun that names the decision logic, then keep the trade-off clause; e.g. "Writing Java capacity-allocation logic that sets upper/lower bounds on EC2 capacity reserved for Amazon Redshift maintenance (e.g. patching), trading availability against cost; initial backtests complete"

bullet_feedback.bullet: Precomputed a category-keyed tree index of popular workflows from a 270K+ row PostgreSQL table (Python/SQLAlchemy, Redis cache) to minimize DB queries under access limits
bullet_feedback.problem: The parenthetical "(Python/SQLAlchemy, Redis cache)" is a tech dump wedged mid-sentence, and "under access limits" does not say whose limits or what kind (rate limits, read quotas, permissions).
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The reason for the design (a constrained shared database) is the interesting engineering decision, but it is the vaguest phrase in the bullet; a reader can restate what was built but not why.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what 'access limits' were (e.g. query/rate limits on a shared PostgreSQL database)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the constraint, then the design, and fold Redis into the sentence as the mechanism rather than a parenthetical; leave SQLAlchemy to the Skills section. e.g. "Because the shared 270K+ row PostgreSQL table was [clarify limit], precomputed a category-keyed tree index of popular workflows in Python and cached it in Redis so lookups rarely hit the database"

bullet_feedback.bullet: Shipped a space-research tool used by Amazon Leo’s public-policy team, now maintained by Leo engineers; deployed on AWS Fargate (Docker) via GitHub Actions and CDK (TypeScript)
bullet_feedback.problem: "space-research tool" does not say what the tool does. The deployment clause also uses bare "CDK" and "GitHub Actions" where screeners match "AWS CDK", "infrastructure as code" and "CI/CD".
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The strongest ownership signal on the page (a tool handed off to and maintained by Amazon engineers) is attached to an unnamed function, and the CI/CD and IaC keywords that backend/cloud postings filter on are present only in forms some matchers miss.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the tool lets the policy team do (search, summarize, track research documents?)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Name the tool's job in a few words, and write the deploy chain in matchable form; e.g. "...deployed on AWS Fargate (Docker) with a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline and AWS CDK (TypeScript) infrastructure as code"

bullet_feedback.bullet: Automated a production EventBridge fine-tuning loop for a Bedrock document-importance classifier, retraining only when a larger LLM’s cross-model eval scores move past a threshold
bullet_feedback.problem: "a larger LLM’s cross-model eval scores move past a threshold" is hard to parse: it is unclear whether the larger model grades the classifier, disagrees with it, or is itself evaluated. "Bedrock" without "Amazon" also misses the exact product term.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The retraining trigger is the design decision an interviewer would ask about, and it is the part a reader cannot restate.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the larger LLM's eval measures (e.g. agreement between its labels and the classifier's)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Spell the trigger as cause and effect, and write "Amazon Bedrock" once; e.g. "...retraining only when a larger LLM, used as a grader, disagrees with the classifier's labels past a set threshold" (adjust to what actually happens)

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built a Python pipeline for PhysTwin (PhD-led digital twin, targeting ICLR) turning AnyGrasp output on multi-camera images into Open3D overlays for a VLM; tuned its prompts to pick correct grasps and judge depth
bullet_feedback.problem: Four proper nouns/acronyms in one line (PhysTwin, AnyGrasp, Open3D, VLM) with "VLM" never expanded; the purpose (a robot choosing how to grasp objects) has to be inferred.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: ATS and LLM screeners match "vision-language model" and "robotics/computer vision"; a recruiter cannot restate what the pipeline is for.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Expand VLM once and state the goal before the tool names; drop one parenthetical. e.g. "Built a Python pipeline for PhysTwin, a PhD-led robotics digital twin targeting ICLR, that renders AnyGrasp grasp candidates from multi-camera images as Open3D overlays so a vision-language model (VLM) can pick the correct grasp; tuned its prompts for grasp choice and depth judgment"

bullet_feedback.bullet: Co-founded a 110+ member campus product studio that has shipped 5 live products, including Tortuga, a class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days; built Redis caching for its Prisma ORM queries
bullet_feedback.problem: Two unrelated claims joined by a semicolon; the candidate's own engineering ("built Redis caching for its Prisma ORM queries") is the tail fragment after the studio's org stats.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A skimming reader credits the 20,000+ visits to the studio, not to the candidate's technical work, and the only backend detail in this role is easy to skip.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Either split into the org fact and the engineering fact, or make the caching the subject: "...including Tortuga, a class scheduler (20,000+ visits in its first 30 days) whose Prisma ORM queries I sped up with a Redis cache"

bullet_feedback.bullet: Building a RAG meal-suggestion feature for the official UMD app (GPT-4o mini, ChromaDB + SentenceBERT search); 93% of generated meals rated satisfactory by internal testers
bullet_feedback.problem: "RAG" is never expanded on the page (also bare in Skills), and the parenthetical is a stack of tool names joined with "+".
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Screeners and non-technical recruiters match "retrieval-augmented generation"; the parenthetical hides how retrieval works (embedding search over a menu/recipe store).
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Expand once and turn the parenthetical into a short clause; e.g. "Building a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) meal-suggestion feature for the official UMD app that retrieves with SentenceBERT embeddings in ChromaDB and generates with GPT-4o mini; ..."

bullet_feedback.bullet: Benchmarked B+ tree vs LSM skip-list stores for the simulation’s event logs on identical 2M-record workloads; the B+ tree gave 12.8× read throughput and 22× faster range summaries for 27% more disk
bullet_feedback.problem: Uses the "×" multiplication glyph and a curly apostrophe; some ATS text pipelines (older Workday/Taleo ingest) render these as "?" or drop them, turning "12.8×" into "12.8".
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Minor: the human reader is fine, but a mangled multiplier in the parsed profile reads as a nonsense number.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Use ASCII "x" ("12.8x", "22x") and a straight apostrophe in the source; otherwise keep the bullet as is.

page_feedback.problem: Education shows only "May 2028" with no "Expected"; parsers (Workday, Greenhouse) store this as a completed graduation date.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Internship postings filter on enrollment and graduation window (e.g. Robinhood: Winter 2027 or Spring 2028; Pinterest: by June 2029); a parsed 'graduated' flag can mis-route the application or trigger a knockout question mismatch.

page_feedback.problem: Several screener-form terms the page already supports are absent in matchable form: "CI/CD" (supported by GitHub Actions deploys), "AWS CDK" / "infrastructure as code" (CDK appears bare), "Amazon Bedrock", "retrieval-augmented generation", "vision-language model", "unit testing" (Jest/Pytest suites), "Git" (GitHub, GitHub Actions).
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Across the postings read (Pinterest, Robinhood backend/web, Lyft backend, Stripe, Notion, Affirm), recurring match terms are Python, Java, TypeScript, React, PostgreSQL, Redis, AWS, testing (unit/integration), CI/CD, data structures, performance and LLM/AI tooling. The resume covers most; the gaps above are wording, not missing experience.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Add them once each, preferably in Skills (e.g. Tools: "Git, GitHub Actions (CI/CD), AWS CDK (infrastructure as code), Docker, Pytest/Jest (unit testing)") and expand acronyms on first use in bullets. Do NOT add Go, Kafka, Kubernetes, Django or REST API design: they appear often in postings but nothing on the page shows that work.

page_feedback.problem: Skills lists items with no supporting bullet: X-Ray, SNS, API Gateway, Node.js, PyTorch, C.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: LLM screeners increasingly cross-check skills against experience and down-weight unsupported lists; an interviewer may open with "tell me about your PyTorch work".
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep each only if the candidate can speak to real use; otherwise cut. This is preferable to adding them to bullets.

page_feedback.problem: Extraction order puts the date and location lines between employer and title ("Amazon Web Services / Sep 2026 – Dec 2026 / Software Development Engineer Intern / Redmond, WA"). Order is consistent across every role, and dates use one format (Mon YYYY – Mon YYYY), so this parses correctly in most systems.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Low risk; noted only because older parsers occasionally attach the title to the wrong employer when a date line intervenes.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: No change needed unless a specific ATS shows mis-parses; if so, keep employer and title on adjacent lines in the source order.

page_feedback.problem: Employer line "UMD App Development Contracting (Client: Amazon Leo)" can be parsed as employer = "Amazon Leo" or the whole string.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: An Amazon recruiter's ATS may show two Amazon employers; harmless, but the contract relationship is the honest framing and should survive parsing.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Fine as is; optionally move the client into the title line ("Software Engineer (Contract), client: Amazon Leo") so the employer field is clean.

page_feedback.problem: Several bullets are compressed with "+", "/" and parentheticals ("React/TypeScript + Electron", "CloudWatch + OpenSearch", "ChromaDB + SentenceBERT", "(Python/SQLAlchemy, Redis cache)").
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Reads as notes rather than sentences (hurts human_voice and plain_language); tokenizers handle it, but LLM screeners summarize these bullets less accurately.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Replace "+" with "and"/"with" and turn parentheticals into clauses where the tool explains the method; move the rest to Skills.

Reduced end-to-end latency 34% for a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research documents to inference by replacing S3 staging hops with Kinesis streams feeding Lambda
Cut LLM workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by decomposing a Claude skill into sub-skills backed by Python search/validation tools, guided by CloudWatch + OpenSearch latency logs
Rebuilt a legacy test-data workflow builder in React/TypeScript + Electron, adding a React-Flow editor and Jest-tested validation; 90% of 30+ surveyed developers preferred it to the old tool
Standard section headings (Education, Experience, Projects, Technical Skills), single-column layout, consistent Mon YYYY – Mon YYYY dates, and plain-text contact line
